title: Lecture 1 — Foundations
description: Foundational questions on the Internet, web standards, networks, protocols, domain names, and markup languages.
subject: Web Development

questions.question: What was the original precursor network to the Internet, funded by the US Department of Defense?
questions.explanation: ARPANET connected academic and military networks and was a precursor to the Internet.

questions.question: The Internet is best described as:
options: A graphical interface for reading documents.
A global system of interconnected networks.
A single server located in the United States.
A private network for academic research.
questions.correctAnswer: A global system of interconnected networks.
questions.explanation: The Internet is a network of interconnected networks, rather than a single computer or the Web interface.

questions.question: Who introduced the World Wide Web in 1990?
questions.explanation: Tim Berners-Lee introduced the World Wide Web, which made hypertext resources accessible over the Internet.

questions.question: The World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) is responsible for:
options: Developing recommendations and standards for web design, such as HTML.
Maintaining the physical fiber-optic cables of the Internet.
questions.correctAnswer: Developing recommendations and standards for web design, such as HTML.
questions.explanation: The W3C develops Web standards, including standards related to HTML and accessibility.

questions.question: Which organization coordinates the assignment of Internet domain names and IP addresses?
questions.explanation: ICANN coordinates domain names and IP addresses.

questions.question: What is the definition of an intranet?
options: A network that securely shares operations with external partners.
A private network contained within an organization to share resources among coworkers.
A network designed for global, public access.
A network restricted entirely to military use.
questions.correctAnswer: A private network contained within an organization to share resources among coworkers.
questions.explanation: An intranet is a private network used within an organization; sharing selected resources externally describes an extranet.

questions.question: "The design of products and environments to be usable by all people, to the greatest extent possible, without the need for adaptation" is the definition of:
questions.explanation: Universal design aims to make products and environments usable by all people without requiring adaptation.

questions.question: In the client/server model, the role of the client is typically to:
options: Fulfill requests and transmit status codes.
Request a service, web page, or file over a network.
Route data packets across different networks.
questions.correctAnswer: Request a service, web page, or file over a network.
questions.explanation: A client, such as a web browser, requests resources from a server.

questions.question: A network usually confined to a single building or group of buildings is called a:
questions.explanation: A local area network (LAN) connects devices in a limited local area.

questions.question: Which protocol breaks files and messages into individual units called packets?
questions.explanation: TCP breaks data into packets and supports reliable delivery; IP routes packets.

questions.question: Which protocol is responsible for routing a packet to the correct destination address?
questions.explanation: IP handles addressing and routing packets to their destination.

questions.question: What does HTTP stand for?
questions.explanation: HTTP is the Hypertext Transfer Protocol, used to exchange Web resources.

questions.question: Which of the following is an email protocol used for sending email?
questions.explanation: SMTP is used to send email; POP3 and IMAP are used to retrieve it.

questions.question: What does the MIME protocol allow email systems to do?
options: Route emails faster than standard TCP/IP.
Include multimedia content like images and attachments.
questions.correctAnswer: Include multimedia content like images and attachments.
questions.explanation: MIME extends email formats to support multimedia and file attachments.

questions.question: A unique numeric address for a device on the Internet, consisting of four octets (for example, 216.58.194.46), is an:
questions.explanation: An IPv4 address is a numeric address used to identify a device on a network.

questions.question: What is the function of the Domain Name System (DNS)?
options: It encrypts data sent between browsers and servers.
It associates text-based domain names with unique computer IP addresses.
It hosts the files for a website.
It provides the graphical user interface for a web browser.
questions.correctAnswer: It associates text-based domain names with unique computer IP addresses.
questions.explanation: DNS resolves human-readable domain names to IP addresses.

questions.question: In the URL `http://www.google.com`, what does `.com` represent?
questions.explanation: The top-level domain is the rightmost part of a domain name, such as `.com`.

questions.question: Which markup language was developed by the W3C to combine the formatting strengths of HTML 4.0 with the data structure strengths of XML?
questions.explanation: XHTML combines HTML conventions with the stricter structure of XML.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of XML?
options: To apply styling and colors to web pages.
To describe, deliver, and exchange structured information.
questions.correctAnswer: To describe, deliver, and exchange structured information.
questions.explanation: XML is designed to describe and exchange structured data, not to style pages.

questions.question: The Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act emphasize the importance of:
options: Strict copyright laws on the Web.
questions.explanation: These laws emphasize making digital services accessible to people with disabilities.
